pr_body:
Closes: #10140

  If you include `Fixes #0000` (replacing `0000` with the issue number)

I'm using typeorm with mysql, all of my code works based on typeorm. 
But when I tried to converting my database to sqlite, I found that with sqlite, timestamp column doesn't work.

```
DataTypeNotSupportedError: Data type "timestamp" in "xxxx" is not supported by "sqlite" database.
```

In this situation I have to change all of my code that using timestamp column. that's why I made this PR.
I made timestamp type work using bigint type with sqlite.

If you have any good idea or advice, let me know.
I'll do my best to fix this issue.
thank you.

> @bejewelkyoungminkim do you mind adding support for other timestamp types? For example, `timestamp with time zone`. Also, at the point of returning the data, can you convert back to `Date`?

`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` this type must be for postgresql. But I'm not using postgresql. Somebody will help

According to https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html SQLite doesn't support timestamp data type. We must only have types supported by underlying database to prevent confusion / possible future types added by the database driver itself.

> Various databases have various types.

Correct, different databases support different types. However, it's up to you how exactly you want to "normalize" the types. Because once you start to "normalize" types manually different use cases and edge cases start to arise and it brings lot of problems. For example, why "timestamp" leads to "bigint"? It's inefficient, let's use some different more effecient type. Some people can complain about it and say "no, we need exactly bigint because it supports numeric operations". Others can say we need to have timestamps as strings to support some string-based operations. This is just a primitive example, variety of issues can be much larger. That's why we keep it up to user to define type normalization. 

> And typeorm already provide a way to normalize columns 

Yes, we do provide opinion-based normalization for JavaScript types, since we support column definition without explicit types defined and set of `simple-*` types as an exception. We don't have plans to extend this list.

> According to https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html SQLite doesn't support timestamp data type. We must only have types supported by underlying database to prevent confusion / possible future types added by the database driver itself.

Sqlite uses Integer to represent Timestamp

```
INTEGER as Unix Time, the number of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.
```

So this normalization is valid, it's even more valid than normalizing `uuid` to `varchar` as typeorm already did

> > Various databases have various types.
> 
> Correct, different databases support different types. However, it's up to you how exactly you want to "normalize" the types. Because once you start to "normalize" types manually different use cases and edge cases start to arise and it brings lot of problems. For example, why "timestamp" leads to "bigint"? It's inefficient, let's use some different more effecient type. Some people can complain about it and say "no, we need exactly bigint because it supports numeric operations". Others can say we need to have timestamps as strings to support some string-based operations. This is just a primitive example, variety of issues can be much larger. That's why we keep it up to user to define type normalization.
> 
> > And typeorm already provide a way to normalize columns
> 
> Yes, we do provide opinion-based normalization for JavaScript types, since we support column definition without explicit types defined and set of `simple-*` types as an exception. We don't have plans to extend this list.

Can we at least have a way to set this up once instead of having to use a transformer for each column in each entity? This would help for situations where you want to run integration tests with SQLite when your production app uses a standard RDBMS like Postgres etc..

> Sqlite uses Integer to represent Timestamp

we didn't get it merged yet, and there is already one thing to debate: integer vs bigint for sqlite timestamps

> So this normalization is valid, it's even more valid than normalizing uuid to varchar as typeorm already did

one another debate opened for uuid normalization implementation. 

See we already have complains about currently implemented normalization strategies.
That's why it's better to keep these decisions to users.

If not to merge this pr is majority, do we have any other solution for this? 
It is hard to find a convenient solution for nestjs+typeorm users.

> but if DATABASE_TYPE is injected when app started, we can't use this way.

I don't understand what you mean here. Why you can't use it such way?

This is specific of your application architecture. If you decide to get value from some `configService` -> you should be able to understand how to access it decorators. If that's something that is not accessible from the root of your file -> you need to take values from the other source / place. Make things simpler and everything will work :)

You can find various ways to make it possible. Yes, I know.
But we have to make lots of decorators with condition or transformers.
I think my solution is best way to prepare hydrated value for "Date" type and timstamp column.

@bejewelkyoungminkim I'm sorry, but this is too much opinionated and we don't want to go such way and have multiple other issues of users complaining about specific behaviors of "normalized opinionated types".

If you have too many conditions in your decorators - consider creating your own decorators and re-use them across your codebase.

issue_context.title: timestamp type column doesn't work when using sqlite
issue_context.body:
### Issue description

timestamp type column doesn't work when using sqlite

### Expected Behavior

``` 
@Entity()
export class Photo {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn({
        type: 'int',
    })
    id: number

    @Column('varchar')
    name: string;

    @Column('timestamp')
    publishedAt: Date
}
```
both mysql-family and sqlite, entity works correctly.

### Actual Behavior

DataTypeNotSupportedError: Data type "timestamp" in "table.column" is not supported by "sqlite" database.

### Steps to reproduce

``` 
@Entity()
export class Photo {
    @PrimaryGeneratedColumn({
        type: 'int',
    })
    id: number

    @Column('varchar')
    name: string;

    @Column('timestamp')
    publishedAt: Date
}
```
just use column decorator using timestamp type.

### My Environment

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    | mac         |
| Node.js version     | 16.x  |
| Typescript version  | 5.x  |
| TypeORM version     | 0.3.4  |


### Additional Context

_No response_

### Are you willing to resolve this issue by submitting a Pull Request?

Yes, I have the time, and I know how to start.
